objective_pt: Soften claims and express degrees of certainty with hedging language ("I'd argue", "to some extent", "it would seem") so you sound measured rather than blunt.

teacher.goal_pt: Notice how blunt statements can sound rude or naive in English and start softening them.
prompts: Is remote work better than working in an office?
How sure are you about that, on a scale from one to ten?
watchFor: Overusing "I think" as the only hedge; push for variety ("I'd say", "I suspect").
Translating "com certeza" as "with certainty" when "definitely" or "for sure" is natural.

exercises.instruction_pt: Repeat, keeping the tone relaxed and tentative.
exercises.prompt: I'd argue that it's not quite that simple.
accepted: I'd argue that it's not quite that simple
I'd argue it's not quite that simple
I would argue that it is not quite that simple

exercises.instruction_pt: Which sentence sounds the most measured in a work meeting?
options: I'm not entirely convinced the plan will work as it stands.
exercises.explanation_pt: "Not entirely convinced" and "as it stands" soften the disagreement and leave room for discussion.

exercises.instruction_pt: Say this in natural English: "Eu diria que isso depende do contexto."
accepted: I'd say that depends on the context
I'd say it depends on the context
I would say it depends on the context
I'd say that it depends on the context
I'd say it depends on context
I'd say that depends on context
I'd say it really depends on the context

commonErrors.explanation_pt: In English it's "depend on", not "depend of" (a literal copy of "depender de").
commonErrors.correction_en: I'd say it depends on the context.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Eu diria" is conditional: use "I'd say" / "I would say", not "I will say".
commonErrors.correction_en: I'd say it depends on the context.

teacher.goal_pt: Build a toolkit of hedges: arguably, to some extent, it would seem, I'm inclined to think, tend to.
prompts: Give me an opinion about social media using "arguably".
What do Brazilians tend to do on weekends?
watchFor: "Tend to" followed by a gerund ("tend to doing") instead of the base verb.

exercises.meaning_pt: possivelmente, pode-se dizer que (com bons argumentos)
exercises.example_en: It's arguably the best coffee in the city.
To some extent, I agree with you.
I'm inclined to think the delay was unavoidable.

exercises.instruction_pt: Match each hedge with its meaning.
Say this in natural English: "Até certo ponto, você tem razão."
accepted: To some extent, you're right
To some extent you have a point
To a certain extent, you're right
To an extent, you're right
You're right to some extent
You're right to a certain extent
Up to a point, you're right
You're right, up to a point
To some degree, you're right

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Ter razão" is "to be right" in English. "You have reason" is a literal translation and sounds wrong.
commonErrors.correction_en: To some extent, you're right.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Até certo ponto" is "to some extent" or "up to a point". "Until" is only for time.
commonErrors.correction_en: To some extent, you're right.

teacher.goal_pt: Practise the falling-rising intonation that signals reservation, and the reduced "would" in "it'd" and "I'd".
prompts: Say "Well... maybe" as if you don't really agree.
Say "It would seem so" quickly and naturally.
watchFor: Flat intonation that makes hedges sound like firm statements.
Pronouncing every syllable of "would" fully in connected speech.

exercises.instruction_pt: Repeat with a fall-rise on "sense" to show reservation.
accepted: In a sense, that's true
In a sense that is true

exercises.prompt: It would seem that we underestimated the costs.
accepted: It would seem that we underestimated the costs
It would seem we underestimated the costs

exercises.instruction_pt: Where is the main stress in "arguably"?
exercises.explanation_pt: Like "argue", the stress falls on the first syllable: AR-gu-a-bly.

teacher.goal_pt: Detect how certain a speaker really is from the hedges they use.
prompts: When someone says "I'm not sure that's the best idea", what do they really mean?
How would you respond to a hedged criticism?
watchFor: Taking polite hedges literally and missing the disagreement behind them.
Answering with a flat "yes" or "no" instead of a hedged reply.

exercises.instruction_pt: Listen. How does the speaker feel about the proposal?
exercises.listen: I can see the appeal, but I'm not sure it's the best use of our budget right now.
options: She has serious doubts about it.
exercises.explanation_pt: "I can see the appeal, but I'm not sure..." is a polite way of disagreeing.

exercises.instruction_pt: Listen and give a cautious, partly agreeing answer.
exercises.listen: Do you think artificial intelligence will replace teachers?
accepted: To some extent, maybe
To some extent, but not entirely
Not entirely, I'd say
I doubt it will replace them completely
I doubt it, at least not completely
Perhaps partly, but not completely
Possibly in some areas, but not entirely
It might, to some extent
I'd say only partly
I don't think it will replace them entirely
I don't think it'll fully replace them
Not completely, I don't think

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Acho que não" is "I don't think so" in English, not "I think no".
commonErrors.correction_en: I don't think so, at least not completely.

exercises.instruction_pt: Listen and answer with a hedge that shows you're fairly but not completely sure.
exercises.listen: Will the project be finished by Friday?
accepted: It should be
It should be, yes
Hopefully
Hopefully, yes
Probably
Most likely
In all likelihood, yes
I'd imagine so
I would think so
I'd expect so
I expect so
I think so, but I can't promise
Probably, but I can't guarantee it

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Espero que sim" is "I hope so" (or "hopefully"), not "I hope yes".
commonErrors.correction_en: Hopefully, yes.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Com certeza" is "definitely" or "for sure"; "with certainty" sounds formal and odd. And here you were asked to hedge, so avoid sounding 100% sure.
commonErrors.correction_en: It should be.

teacher.goal_pt: Hold an opinion while sounding open-minded: hedge, give a reason, concede a point.
prompts: Should companies require employees to return to the office?
What are the downsides of your view?
Is there anything you're less sure about?
watchFor: "In my opinion, I think..." (double hedge); one is enough.

exercises.instruction_pt: Say this in natural English: "Não tenho tanta certeza de que isso seja uma boa ideia."

I'm not so sure that it's a good idea
I'm not so sure that's such a good idea

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Ter certeza" is "to be sure": "I'm not sure", not "I don't have certainty".
commonErrors.correction_en: I'm not so sure that's a good idea.

exercises.instruction_pt: Say this in natural English: "Atualmente, a maioria das pessoas tende a trabalhar de casa."
accepted: Nowadays, most people tend to work from home
These days, most people tend to work from home
Currently, most people tend to work from home
At the moment, most people tend to work from home
Most people tend to work from home nowadays
Most people tend to work from home these days

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Actually" means "na verdade", not "atualmente". Use "nowadays", "these days" or "currently".
commonErrors.correction_en: Nowadays, most people tend to work from home.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: For people in general, say "most people" without "of the".
commonErrors.correction_en: Nowadays, most people tend to work from home.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Tend to" is followed by the base form: "tend to work".
commonErrors.correction_en: Nowadays, most people tend to work from home.

exercises.instruction_pt: Role-play: respond to your friend with nuance. Agree partly, then qualify.
exercises.scene_pt: A friend makes a sweeping claim about social media over coffee.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.text: Honestly, I think social media has ruined our ability to concentrate.

turns.speaker: you
turns.cue_pt: Agree to some extent, but say it's not quite that simple.
accepted: To some extent, but I think it's not quite that simple
To some extent, yes, but it's not quite that simple
I agree to some extent, but it's not quite that simple
Up to a point, but it's not quite that simple
You have a point, but it's not quite that simple
To an extent, but it's not that simple
I'd agree to some extent, but it's not quite that simple

commonErrors.explanation_pt: The preposition is "to": "to some extent", "to a certain extent".
commonErrors.correction_en: To some extent, yes.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.text: Come on. Everyone's glued to their phones these days.

turns.speaker: you
turns.cue_pt: Say that's true by and large, but some people use it to learn.
accepted: By and large that's true, but some people use it to learn
That's true by and large, but some people use it to learn
That's largely true, but some people use it to learn
That's true on the whole, but some people use it to learn
By and large, yes, but some people use it to learn things
On the whole that's true, but some people use it for learning
That's broadly true, but some people use it to learn

commonErrors.explanation_pt: After "for" use -ing ("for learning"), or use "to learn".
commonErrors.correction_en: Some people use it to learn.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.text: Fair enough. So what would you say the real problem is?

turns.speaker: you
turns.cue_pt: Say you'd argue the problem is how we use it, not the technology itself.
accepted: I'd argue the problem is how we use it, not the technology itself
I'd argue that the problem is how we use it, not the technology itself
I would argue the problem is how we use it, not the technology itself
I'd argue it's how we use it, not the technology itself
I'd argue the problem is the way we use it, not the technology itself
I'd say the problem is how we use it, not the technology itself

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "A própria tecnologia" is "the technology itself", not "the own technology".
commonErrors.correction_en: Not the technology itself.

exercises.instruction_pt: Answer the question in about a minute. Take a position, but hedge it and concede at least one point.
exercises.prompt_en: Some people say a four-day working week would make everyone more productive. What's your take on that?
guidelines_pt: Open with a hedge: "I'd be inclined to think..." or "To some extent...".
Give one reason and one example.
Close with a qualified conclusion: "On balance, ...".

teacher.goal_pt: Recycle the hedges and check that the learner can switch between firm and tentative statements.
prompts: Make this softer: "That's a bad idea."
Make this firmer: "It might possibly be a problem."
watchFor: Stacking too many hedges ("maybe perhaps possibly"), which sounds evasive.

exercises.instruction_pt: Make this sentence more tentative and say it: "This plan will fail."

commonErrors.explanation_pt: That's the original, blunt version. Add a modal ("might", "could") or a softener ("I suspect...").

accepted: on
upon

practice.instruction_pt: Answer in about a minute. Give your view, but hedge where you are not sure.
practice.prompt_en: Will remote work still be common ten years from now?

practice.instruction_pt: Role-play: answer your colleague with measured, hedged language.
practice.scene_pt: A colleague asks what you think of a new supplier's proposal. You have some doubts.

practice.instruction_pt: Which reply sounds the most measured?
options: Yes, absolutely, no doubt about it.

practice.instruction_pt: Which sentence expresses the highest degree of certainty?
